function_name: __Adminable_init
code: function __Adminable_init() public virtual initializer {
        OwnableUpgradeable.__Ownable_init();
        AccessControlUpgradeable.__AccessControl_init();
        _setupRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, _msgSender());
    }
vulnerability: Unprotected public initializer allows anyone to become owner and admin
reason: The __Adminable_init function is declared public and only protected by the initializer modifier. If the contract or its proxy is deployed without atomically calling this initializer in the same transaction, an attacker can front-run the legitimate initialization call and execute __Adminable_init first. This sets the attacker as both the owner and the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, granting them full privileged access to all functions protected by onlyOwnerOrAdmin. Additionally, because there is no constructor calling _disableInitializers(), the implementation contract itself can be initialized by an attacker, potentially enabling further attacks if the implementation contains self-destruct or delegatecall functionality. The correct practice is to make base initializers internal and expose a single public initializer in the final contract, and to call _disableInitializers() in the constructor of the implementation.
------------------
